To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the airway and respiratory tissue mechanics of bronchoconstricted cynomolgus macaque monkeys are similar to the mechanics of asthmatic humans, as determined by respiratory system input and transfer impedances.

AS bronchoconstriction in cynomolgus macaques results in a heterogeneous constriction of airways that is associated with an increase of airway wall shunt resistance and a decrease of the lung parenchymal effective compliance.

AS bronchoconstriction in nonhuman primatemodels human asthma in that 1) the changes in lung mechanical parameters (i.e., Raw and Eti) are similar, 2) AS challenge produces predominantly an increase in airway resistance, not tissue elastance, and 3), at higher AS doses (0.5 mg/kg), there is evidence of airway wall shunt.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a nonhuman primate model of asthma.
developing and applying new techniques that will allow us to better understand the pathophysiology of asthma.
the development and application of a new method for the noninvasive measurement of respiratory mechanical properties from respiratory system input or transfer impedance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AS model of asthma provides a good model of the disease, but it is not perfect.

AS challenge in cynomolgus monkey is a useful model of human asthma and that Zin and Zin-based estimates of airway and tissue mechanics are useful in characterizing the mechanical properties of the lung in this model.
the AS model is a good model of human asthma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

AS challenge in cynomolgus monkey produces airway constriction, which results in heterogeneous airway closure, and that Raw and Eti estimated from input and transfer impedance are similar in the baseline state but not in the bronchoconstricted state.
Zin is more appropriate than Ztr for estimating airway resistance and that Ztr is more appropriate than either Zin or Ztr for estimating tissue elastance.
AS inhalation in monkeys induces bronchoconstriction, airway wall shunt, and heterogeneous airway narrowing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Zin and Zti are useful for estimating airway and tissue mechanical properties, but that the properties estimated from the two measurements may be significantly different.
Zin can be used to estimate Raw and Eti, but Ztr should be used to estimate Eti only in the presence of airway shunting.
the respiratory system input impedance is not a reliable measure of lung tissue properties in asthmatic monkeys.
